The '''2002–03 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 101st season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 71st in a [[round-robin tournament]]. It was composed by 18 teams, for the 15th consecutive time from season 1988–89.

The first two teams qualified directly to [[UEFA Champions League]]. Teams finishing in third and fourth position had to play Champions League qualifications. Teams finishing in fifth and sixth positions qualified to [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] (another spot was given to the winner of [[Coppa Italia]]). The bottom four teams were to be relegated in [[Serie B]].

[[Juventus FC|Juventus]] won its 27th national title, with [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] placing second and [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] third. [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] was admitted to the UEFA Champions League preliminary phase, whereas [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]], [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] and [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] (through the Coppa Italia finals) obtained a spot to the next UEFA Cup. [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] and [[A.C. Perugia Calcio|Perugia]] were admitted to participate in the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]], after [[A.C. ChievoVerona|Chievo]] declined to participate.

[[Piacenza Calcio 1919|Piacenza]], [[Torino F.C.|Torino]], [[Como 1907|Como]] and [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] were relegated to [[Serie B]], with the latter after having lost a relegation play-off against [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]].

==Rule changes==
Unlike [[La Liga]], which imposed a quota on the number of non-EU players on each club, Serie A clubs could sign as many non-EU players as available on domestic transfer. But for the [[2003–04 Serie A|2003–04 season]] a quota was imposed on each of the clubs limiting the number of non-[[European Union|EU]], non-[[EFTA]] and non-[[Switzerland|Swiss]] players who may be signed from abroad each season,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=57329.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604164303/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=57329.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=Italy blocks non-EU players|date=2003-03-05|access-date=2010-03-09|publisher=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> following provisional measures<ref name=provision>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=28321.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604164248/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=ita/news/newsid=28321.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 4, 2011|title=Italians bar non-EU imports|date=2002-07-17|access-date=2010-03-09|publisher=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> introduced in the 2002–03 season, which allowed Serie A & B clubs to sign only one non-EU player in the 2002 summer transfer window.

==Teams==
Eighteen teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top fourteen teams from the previous season and the four teams promoted from the [[2001–02 Serie B|Serie B]]. The promoted teams were [[Como 1907|Como]], [[Modena FC 2018|Modena]], [[AS Reggina 1914|Reggina]] and [[Empoli FC|Empoli]]. Como, Modena, Reggina and Empoli returned to the top flight after an absence of thirteen, thirty-eight, one and three years respectively. They replaced [[Hellas Verona]] and [[US Lecce|Lecce]] (both teams relegated after a three-years presence), [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] (relegated after eight season in top fight), and [[Venezia FC|Venezia]] (relegated after a season's presence).

==Overall==
*Most wins - [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] (21)
*Fewest wins - [[Como 1907|Como]] and [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] (4)
*Most draws -  [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] and [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] (15)
*Fewest draws - [[Piacenza Calcio 1919|Piacenza]] (6)
*Most losses - [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] (21)
*Fewest losses - [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] (4)
*Most goals scored - [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] (64)
*Fewest goals scored - [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] (23)
*Most goals conceded - [[Piacenza Calcio 1919|Piacenza]] (62)
*Fewest goals conceded - [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] (29)
